text:
Will Smith is doing most things right and getting little for it. San Jose's 21-year-old plays more than 19 minutes a night, and the Sharks are 4.4 points better in expected-goal share (a measure of who gets the better chances) with him on the ice than without. The problem is the finishing around him: with Smith out there, San Jose has scored 6.2 fewer goals than its chances deserved, the main reason he sits at 11 points in 18 games. That kind of gap usually swings back.

His own game travels. Corey Sznajder's All Three Zones tracking had him in the 98th percentile last season for chances from the home plate in front of the net, and he carries the puck into the zone far more often than he dumps it. The two-goal night that beat Vancouver on Oct. 29 was the glimpse. The open question is defense, where Evolving-Hockey had opponents getting more with him on the ice last season than against most forwards. Our projection's middle case is about 63 more points the rest of the way, which tells you how much we think is coming.
headline: Doing the work, waiting on the payoff
